## What “multi-vector” means

A multi-vector embedding model represents a document as multiple vectors—often one per token or passage segment—rather than compressing it into one dense vector. At retrieval time, it can compare a query’s token vectors against document token vectors, typically offering finer-grained matching than a single-vector embedding.

One established Hugging Face model in this category is **BAAI/bge-m3**. Its model card states that it supports dense retrieval, multi-vector/ColBERT-style retrieval, and sparse retrieval in one model; it has 1,024-dimensional dense embeddings and supports sequences up to 8,192 tokens.[1]
